newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Swiss Clariant's 1996 net jumps 29 percent.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swiss Clariant's 1996 net jumps 29 percent.

text.p: Specialty chemicals maker Clariant AG, spun off by Sandoz ahead of the Novartis megamerger, said its 1996 net profit jumped 29 percent ahead of a planned acquisition from Germany's Hoechst AG.
Clariant on Friday reported net profit of 137 million Swiss francs ($95.5 million) on sales of 2.33 billion francs, up nine percent from 1995.

Clariant's board proposed a dividend of 10 Swiss francs per share for 1996 results as against 4.50 francs for the second half of 1995, when it was created. All 1995 figures were pro forma because Clariant went independent as of July 1 that year.
"The first quarter (of 1997) is good, we are ahead of last year in all divisions," Clariant chief executive Martin Syz told its annual news conference.
Syz also said the outlook for the year was generally positive but did not elaborate.

Despite stiff global competition, Clariant said sales growth was achieved by all of its business areas -- textile, leather and paper dyes and chemicals, as well as pigments and additives and masterbatches for other chemical processors.
"The operating margin also rose from 9.8 percent to 10.1 percent," it said in a statement on its 1996 results.
Operating profit for 1996 rose 11 percent to 235 million Swiss francs and had continued to grow in the first two months of this year, it added.

Clariant's debut in 1995 was followed last year by a another Swiss chemicals newcomer, Ciba Specialty Chemicals AG, also born of a spin-off ahead of the Ciba-Geigy merger with Sandoz that created the world's biggest pharmaceuticals and life sciences group.

Clariant plans to grow next by taking over the specialty chemicals business of German pharmaceutical group Hoechst AG by July 1 retroactive to the start of this year, pending approval from shareholders of both compnaies and regulatory agencies.
Under the plan announced last December, Hoechst will sell its specialty chemicals business HSC in return for a 45 percent stake in the expanded Clariant and cash.
"It is Hoechst's intention to participate in Clariant's future economic success primarily as a passive investor, without influencing the management and its decisions," the Clariant statement said.

To that end, Hoechst's voting rights will be capped at between 10 and 33.4 percent of capital and Hoechst will also have to consult Clariant's board before selling any shares until the year 2005, Clariant said. Hoechst's stake will be created with a new issue of 3.27 million shares.
"Geographically, HSC's South American presence will complement Clariant's established strength in the Asia Pacific region," the statement said.
Clariant executives said they expected the combination with HSC to result in synergies saving some 500 million Swiss francs over a period of two and a half to three years.

"Expansion as such is the strategic priority of the new company, either by better exploitation of the opportunities at the new divisions or by adding businesses," Clariant chairman Rolf Schweizer told Reuters.
The combined company as it currently stands would have sales of some 8.9 billion Swiss francs, making it a world leader in the specialty chemcials sector.
But Schweizer said that figure should change somewhat as a result of synergy effects, rationalisation and the possible divestiture or swap of some operations.
Clariant also plans a 500 million franc provision for restructuring costs and to write-off acquisition goodwill of some 1.6 billion francs over a period of about 20 years. ($ = 1.434 Swiss Francs)
